body_markdown:
Confirming an earlier report, Stellantis has verified that it will shut down most of its factory-backed racing programs over the coming years. The decision affects the group’s participation in several race series, including the World Endurance Championship.


Peugeot will stop racing in the World Endurance Championship, which includes[the 24 Hours of Le Mans](https://www.hagerty.com/media/motorsports/grid-walk-24-hours-of-le-mans-2025/) , after the 2026 season. The brand returned to the series in 2022 after a decade-long hiatus. Citroën and Opel will leave Formula E at the end of the 13th season, which ends in 2027.[Dodge’s long-awaited NASCAR return](https://www.hagerty.com/media/motorsports/its-official-dodge-will-jump-back-into-nascar-cup-racing/) , which was recently announced, is safe, a spokesperson for the brand confirmed to *Hagerty* . “There are no changes to Stellantis North America Motorsports programs,” the spokesperson added.


Exiting factory-backed racing is a way for Stellantis, which owns 14 car brands, to free up resources. The company explained that it will use the money saved to develop new products, improve quality, and expand its market coverage. Stellantis is planning[a big product offensive](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/stellantis-new-model-pipeline-srt-jeep-dodge-ram/) that includes enthusiast-focused models from Jeep, Dodge, and Ram, a born-again Dodge Dakota midsize pickup, and[three new Chrysler crossovers](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/chrysler-airflow-preview/) . All told, the group will invest billions of dollars to launch at least 11 new cars in the United States by 2030.


The pull-back from motorsports allows Stellantis to direct those resources into new models, including a handful for the Chrysler brand, one of which should look like the crossover on the left.


Chrysler


The decision doesn’t mean that Stellantis-owned carmakers will no longer be able to use the term “racing-inspired” as a marketing tool. Stellantis Motorsport is sticking around, and it will leverage its expertise to “further strengthen customer racing activities,” the brand explained. As of writing, Peugeot, Citroën, and Lancia sell turn-key race cars built to Rally2 and Rally4 specifications.


Stellantis Motorsport also clarified that it remains committed to helping develop performance cars for Alfa Romeo and Maserati, among other brands. The storied Veloce (Alfa Romeo), GTi (Peugeot), HF (Lancia), and GSE (Opel) nameplates will live on.


While racing fans will undoubtedly be disappointed to see the Le Mans grid shrink, the good news is that Stellantis intends to keep every employee affected by the decision to stop racing. They’ll be offered positions in other departments within the company.
